findings.title: OS command injection via unsanitized argv[1] in vuln_path
data_flow: argv[1] copied unchecked into buf via strcpy
buf formatted unchecked into cmd via snprintf
findings.security_condition: attacker-controlled argv[1] reaches system() with no sanitization
findings.exploitability: any caller-supplied argv[1] containing shell metacharacters executes arbitrary commands
findings.why_vulnerable: no length check, no shell-metacharacter escaping before system()
findings.why_not_false_positive: direct, unguarded data flow from parameter to system() with no intervening validation
recommended_next_analysis: confirm dynamically with a crafted argv[1] payload

findings.title: Candidate command execution in safe_path (expected: refuted)
data_flow: argv[1] copied bounds-checked into buf via strncpy
buf is never referenced by the system() call, which uses a fixed string literal
findings.security_condition: argv[1] does NOT reach the system() call at all -- the command argument is a constant
findings.exploitability: none established -- the sink's argument does not depend on the source
findings.impact: none if the flow is genuinely absent, as claimed
findings.why_vulnerable: flagged defensively due to co-located strncpy + system() calls in the same function
findings.why_not_false_positive: included to exercise the verifier's REFUTED path -- a real analyst would likely have discarded this, but it is a legitimate reachability question for Joern to settle
recommended_next_analysis: confirm via CPG dataflow query that buf never reaches the system() argument

analysis_limitations: Synthetic fixture source written for Stage 5 integration testing -- not real firmware.
